memory_lessons.applicability: CTA-level compact source tiling in this campaign; use the 224-thread result to test whether the 192-to-256 trend continues.
memory_lessons.claim: Valid compact-tile candidates at 128, 160, 192, and 256 threads had different measured means, with 128 threads currently best. These measurements do not support assuming that increasing tile width improves performance.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the official 224-thread result with the measured neighboring settings; if it is not competitive, test a contrasting source-staging strategy rather than merely renaming a tile size.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured compact 128-thread tile is currently best at 0.00089008 s, while compact 160-, 192-, and 256-thread candidates measured 0.00092808, 0.00092263, and 0.00091997 s. With nine distinct prior programs and no repeats, this candidate tests a new 224-thread CTA/tile between the 192- and 256-thread settings. Each thread still computes one target, and its 224 compact source records use 3,584 bytes of shared memory. The measurements are non-monotonic, so no speedup is assumed.

retained: Set block and items_per_block to 224 so each thread remains responsible for exactly one target and the staged source tile matches the CTA width.
Stage only source x, y, z, and mass in 16-byte shared-memory records, allocating 3,584 bytes per CTA.
Handle partial source tiles and output bounds while keeping all threads at both CTA-wide barriers and preserving source interaction order and force arithmetic.
